panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient showing symmetric, well-demarcated erythematous plaques involving both buttocks in a butterfly/V-shaped distribution across the gluteal cleft. The caption and in-text explicitly link this eruption to amoxicillin drug provocation in a patient with SDRIFE (article title), and the gluteal/intertriginous involvement with bilateral symmetry matches the disease's classic presentation. No other disease is mentioned for this panel and no third-party copyright is indicated.
panels.attribution_text: Letón-Cabanillas et al. Symmetrical Drug-Related Intertriginous and Flexural Exanthema With Amoxicillin: Presenting a Flare-Up Phenomenon.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.74393. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Bilateral gluteal erythematous plaques following positive amoxicillin drug provocation test
in_text_mentions: d amoxicillin extract (20 mg/mL) (Lab Diater®, Madrid, Spain), was performed with negative readings at 15 minutes and 24 hours. Therefore, a DPT with amoxicillin was initiated following our protocol for delayed reactions. On the first day, half of the minimum effective dose (250 mg) was administered. The following day, the full dose (500 mg) was given. Subsequently, the patient continued with home treatment at a dosage of 500 mg every 12 hours. After three days of home treatment, the patient experienced bilateral pruritic and erythematous plaques in the gluteal and inguinal regions (Figure 1).

in_text_mentions: In her previous flares, inverse psoriasis had typically manifested as well-demarcated erythematous patches within axillae, groin, and inframammary folds, without appreciable scaling owing to constant flexural moisture. In contrast, the current eruption showed well-defined, symmetrical erythema accompanied by superficial desquamation involving the groin, axillae, inframammary areas, and lower abdomen (Figure 2).

She reported mild pruritus and a burning sensation without mucosal involvement or systemic symptoms.

plate_findings.evidence: bilateral, symmetrical, well-demarcated blue-purple macules and plaques involving the axillary, flexures of the extremities, inguinal, and gluteal regions

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A captioned as flexural forearm SDRIFE exanthema in article titled Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid-Induced Symmetric Drug-Related Intertrigious and Flexural Exanthema with in-text symmetrical well-demarcated flexural macules/plaques. B: Panel B captioned as axillar area SDRIFE exanthema with matching in-text bilateral symmetrical axillary macules/plaques. C: Panel C captioned as posterior neck SDRIFE exanthema with in-text posterior neck involvement with symmetrical macules/plaques. D: Panel D captioned as inguinal region SDRIFE exanthema (caption typo second C) with matching in-text symmetrical inguinal macules/plaques.
panels.attribution_text: Alpagat et al. Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid-Induced Symmetric Drug-Related Intertrigious and Flexural Exanthema.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.33849. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Skin exanthema of various sites due to SDRIFE (A: Flexural forearm, B: Axillar area, C: Posterior neck, C: Inguinal region).
in_text_mentions: Dermatological examination of the posterior neck and the intertriginous area revealed many bilateral, symmetrical, well-demarcated blue-purple macules and plaques involving the axillary, flexures of the extremities, inguinal, and gluteal regions (Figure 1). In the form of pustules, papules, purpura or bullae. There were no skin lesions on the palms, soles, or mucosae. A systemic analysis turned out nothing unusual. Urinalysis results and blood cell counts were both normal. For a superficial fungal infection, direct microscopic inspection and culture produced negative results.
